lessons.title: Greet and Introduce Yourself
lessons.description: Learn basic greetings and how to introduce yourself to new people in English.

sections.heading: Clear Pronunciation of Greetings
sections.content: Practice saying 'Hello' and 'Hi' clearly. The 'h' in 'Hello' is a soft sound, like a gentle breath. The 'i' in 'Hi' is a long 'eye' sound.

sections.heading: Introducing Your Name
sections.content: Use simple phrases like: 'Hello, my name is [Your Name].' or 'Hi, I'm [Your Name].' For example: 'Hello, my name is Mai.' or 'Hi, I'm Nam.'

sections.heading: Keep it Simple
sections.content: At A1, focus on short, complete sentences. Don't try to say too much. A simple greeting and your name are perfect for a first introduction.

sections.heading: Practice Your Own Introduction
sections.content: Say your full introduction out loud several times. This builds confidence and helps you speak more smoothly when you meet someone new.

mcqQuestions.stemText: What do you say when you meet someone for the first time?
Choose the correct word: 'My name _____ Linh.'
How do you ask someone's name?

speakingTasks.prompt: Introduce yourself. Say 'Hello', state your name, and mention one simple thing about yourself (e.g., 'I am a student'). Speak for 30-45 seconds.
Imagine you are meeting a new classmate. Greet them and introduce yourself, then ask 'What is your name?'. Speak for 30-45 seconds.

lessons.title: Talk About Your Family
lessons.description: Learn to describe your family members and talk about them using simple English phrases.

sections.heading: Pronouncing Plurals for Family Members
sections.content: When talking about more than one person, add an 's'. Practice 'brothers' (sounds like 'z') and 'sisters' (sounds like 'z'). The 's' in 'parents' also sounds like 'z'.

sections.heading: Describing Your Family Structure
sections.content: Use 'I have...' or 'There are...' For example: 'I have one brother and one sister.' or 'There are four people in my family: my mother, my father, my brother, and me.'

sections.heading: Use Simple Adjectives
sections.content: Describe your family members with easy words like 'tall', 'short', 'nice', 'kind', 'funny'. For example: 'My mother is kind.' or 'My brother is tall.'

sections.heading: Connect Ideas with 'and'
sections.content: To make your sentences longer, use 'and'. For example: 'I have a mother and a father.' or 'My sister is smart and funny.'

mcqQuestions.stemText: Your mother's brother is your _____.
Choose the correct plural: 'I have two _____.'
My family _____ big.

speakingTasks.prompt: Describe your immediate family. Mention how many people are in your family and name your closest family members (e.g., mother, father, siblings). Speak for 30-45 seconds.
Choose one family member you like very much. Describe them with two simple adjectives and say one reason why you like them. Speak for 30-45 seconds.

lessons.title: Describe Your Home
lessons.description: Learn how to talk about your home, including its type and the rooms inside.

sections.heading: Pronouncing 'There is' and 'There are'
sections.content: Practice 'There is' (for one item) and 'There are' (for multiple items). Make sure the 'th' sound is clear, and the 's' in 'is' sounds like 'z'.

sections.heading: Common Phrases for Describing Home
sections.content: Use: 'I live in a house/apartment.' 'My home has [number] rooms.' 'There is a living room, a kitchen, and a bedroom.' For example: 'I live in an apartment. It has three rooms.'

sections.heading: Use Prepositions of Place
sections.content: Use simple prepositions like 'in' or 'on' to describe where things are. For example: 'My bed is in my bedroom.' or 'There is a TV in the living room.'

sections.heading: Start with General, then Specific
sections.content: Begin by saying what type of home you live in, then talk about the number of rooms, and finally mention one or two specific rooms.

mcqQuestions.stemText: Which room is typically used for sleeping?
Choose the correct phrase: '_____ a big garden behind my house.'
I live _____ an apartment.

speakingTasks.prompt: Describe your home. Say if you live in a house or an apartment, and mention how many rooms it has. Name two rooms in your home. Speak for 30-45 seconds.
Talk about your favorite room in your home. What is it? What do you do there? Speak for 30-45 seconds.

lessons.title: Your Favorite Food
lessons.description: Learn to talk about your favorite food and why you like it using simple English.

sections.heading: Pronouncing Food Names Clearly
sections.content: Practice saying the names of common foods like 'pizza', 'noodles', 'rice', 'chicken'. Pay attention to the vowel sounds. For example, 'rice' has a long 'i' sound.

sections.heading: Expressing Preferences
sections.content: Use 'My favorite food is...' or 'I like...' For example: 'My favorite food is pho.' or 'I like pizza very much.'

sections.heading: Simple Reasons for Liking Food
sections.content: Give a very simple reason: 'It is delicious.' 'It is sweet.' 'It is healthy.' For example: 'I like apples. They are sweet and healthy.'

sections.heading: Use 'and' to Add Details
sections.content: You can combine ideas with 'and'. For example: 'I like chicken and rice.' or 'My favorite food is pho, and it is very delicious.'

mcqQuestions.stemText: Which word describes food that tastes good?
My favorite food _____ pizza.
I like fruit because it is _____.

speakingTasks.prompt: Talk about your favorite food. What is it? Why do you like it? Give one simple reason. Speak for 30-45 seconds.
Describe two foods you like and one food you don't like. Use simple adjectives to describe them. Speak for 30-45 seconds.

lessons.title: Describe a Pet or Animal
lessons.description: Learn to describe a pet or an animal using basic English vocabulary and phrases.

sections.heading: Pronouncing Animal Names
sections.content: Practice saying common animal names like 'dog', 'cat', 'fish', 'bird'. Pay attention to the short vowel sounds, e.g., 'o' in 'dog' and 'a' in 'cat'.

sections.heading: Describing an Animal's Appearance
sections.content: Use 'It is...' or 'It has...' For example: 'It is a dog. It is brown and white.' or 'It has big eyes and a long tail.'

sections.heading: Use Simple Adjectives for Description
sections.content: Use words like 'big', 'small', 'cute', 'fast', 'slow' to describe the animal. For example: 'My cat is small and cute.'

sections.heading: Mention What it Does
sections.content: You can add a simple action the animal does. For example: 'My dog likes to play.' or 'Birds can fly.'

mcqQuestions.stemText: Which animal says 'meow'?
A cat _____ four legs.
My dog is very _____ and likes to run.

speakingTasks.prompt: Describe a pet you have or an animal you like. What kind of animal is it? What color is it? Is it big or small? Speak for 30-45 seconds.
Talk about what your favorite animal likes to do. Does it play? Does it eat specific food? Speak for 30-45 seconds.

lessons.title: Talk About School
lessons.description: Learn to talk about your school, your favorite subjects, and what you do there.

sections.heading: Pronouncing 'School' and 'Subject'
sections.content: Practice 'school' (long 'oo' sound) and 'subject' (stress on the first syllable). Make sure the 's' sound is clear.

sections.heading: Talking About School Activities
sections.content: Use 'I go to school.' 'I study [subject].' 'My favorite subject is [subject].' For example: 'I go to primary school. My favorite subject is English.'

sections.heading: Use Simple Verbs
sections.content: Use verbs like 'study', 'learn', 'play', 'read' to describe what you do at school. For example: 'I learn math at school.' or 'I play with friends.'

sections.heading: Mention People at School
sections.content: You can briefly mention 'teachers' and 'friends'. For example: 'I have good teachers.' or 'I play with my friends at school.'

mcqQuestions.stemText: Which subject teaches you about numbers?
I _____ to school every day.
My favorite _____ is science.

speakingTasks.prompt: Talk about your school. What is its name? What grade are you in? What is one subject you study? Speak for 30-45 seconds.
Describe your favorite subject at school. Why do you like it? What do you learn in it? Speak for 30-45 seconds.

lessons.title: Describe the Weather
lessons.description: Learn to talk about different types of weather and how you feel about them.

sections.heading: Pronouncing Weather Words
sections.content: Practice 'sunny', 'rainy', 'cloudy', 'cold', 'hot'. Pay attention to the 'y' sound at the end of many weather adjectives, which sounds like 'ee'.

sections.heading: Talking About Today's Weather
sections.content: Use 'It is...' For example: 'It is sunny today.' or 'It is rainy and cold.' You can also say 'The weather is nice/bad.'

sections.heading: Expressing Feelings About Weather
sections.content: Say 'I like...' or 'I don't like...' For example: 'I like sunny weather.' or 'I don't like rainy days.'

sections.heading: Connect Weather to Activities
sections.content: Briefly mention what you do in certain weather. For example: 'When it is sunny, I play outside.' or 'When it is rainy, I read a book.'

mcqQuestions.stemText: What kind of weather has a lot of water falling from the sky?
It is very _____ today. I need a jacket.
The sun is shining. It is a _____ day.

speakingTasks.prompt: Describe the weather today. Is it sunny, rainy, or cloudy? Is it hot or cold? Speak for 30-45 seconds.
Talk about your favorite type of weather. Why do you like it? What do you like to do when the weather is like that? Speak for 30-45 seconds.

lessons.title: Your Daily Routine
lessons.description: Learn to talk about your daily activities from morning to evening using simple time expressions.

sections.heading: Pronouncing Verbs Clearly
sections.content: Practice common verbs like 'get up', 'eat', 'go', 'study', 'sleep'. Pay attention to the final consonant sounds.

sections.heading: Sequencing Daily Activities
sections.content: Use 'First, I...', 'Then, I...', 'After that, I...', 'Finally, I...'. For example: 'First, I wake up. Then, I eat breakfast. After that, I go to school.'

sections.heading: Use Simple Time Expressions
sections.content: Use 'in the morning', 'in the afternoon', 'in the evening', 'at night'. For example: 'In the morning, I eat breakfast.' or 'In the evening, I do my homework.'

sections.heading: Keep Sentences Short and Direct
sections.content: At A1, it's best to use one simple action per sentence. 'I wake up. I brush my teeth. I eat breakfast.'

mcqQuestions.stemText: What do you usually do before going to school?
I _____ my teeth every morning.
After school, I usually _____ my homework.

speakingTasks.prompt: Describe your daily routine. Talk about three things you do in the morning and two things you do in the afternoon or evening. Speak for 30-45 seconds.
Talk about your favorite part of the day. What do you do during that time, and why do you like it? Speak for 30-45 seconds.

lessons.title: Describe Colors Around You
lessons.description: Learn to identify and describe the colors of objects in your environment.

sections.heading: Pronouncing Color Names
sections.content: Practice saying basic colors: 'red', 'blue', 'green', 'yellow', 'black', 'white'. Pay attention to the vowel sounds and final consonants.

sections.heading: Describing Object Colors
sections.content: Use 'It is [color].' or 'The [object] is [color].' For example: 'My bag is blue.' or 'The apple is red and green.'

sections.heading: Look Around You
sections.content: To practice, look at objects in your room or outside and say their colors. 'The wall is white.' 'The book is red.'

sections.heading: Combine Colors with 'and'
sections.content: If an object has two colors, use 'and'. For example: 'My shirt is blue and white.'

mcqQuestions.stemText: What color is the sky on a clear day?
A banana is usually _____.
My shoes are _____ and white.

speakingTasks.prompt: Look around your room. Describe the color of three different objects you see (e.g., 'My chair is brown.'). Speak for 30-45 seconds.
Talk about your favorite color. What is it? Name one or two things that are that color. Speak for 30-45 seconds.

lessons.title: Talk About a Friend
lessons.description: Learn to describe a friend, their appearance, and what you like about them.

sections.heading: Pronouncing Descriptive Adjectives
sections.content: Practice words like 'tall', 'short', 'kind', 'funny'. Pay attention to the 'll' sound in 'tall' and the 'y' sound in 'funny'.

sections.heading: Introducing a Friend
sections.content: Use 'I have a friend. His/Her name is [Name].' or 'My friend [Name] is...' For example: 'I have a friend. Her name is Hoa. She is kind.'

sections.heading: Describe Appearance Simply
sections.content: Use 'He/She has...' for features like hair and eyes. 'He has short hair.' 'She has big eyes.' Use 'He/She is...' for height. 'He is tall.'

sections.heading: Say What You Do Together
sections.content: Mention a simple activity you do with your friend. 'We play together.' 'We study together.'

mcqQuestions.stemText: A person who is always happy and makes you laugh is _____.
My friend _____ long hair.
We like to _____ together after school.

speakingTasks.prompt: Describe one of your friends. What is their name? Is your friend a boy or a girl? Describe their appearance with two simple words (e.g., tall, short, long hair). Speak for 30-45 seconds.
Talk about why you like your friend. What is one good quality they have? What do you like to do together? Speak for 30-45 seconds.

lessons.title: Your Favorite Game
lessons.description: Learn to talk about your favorite game, how to play it, and why you enjoy it.

sections.heading: Pronouncing Game Names
sections.content: Practice saying the names of games clearly, whether they are traditional games or video games. For example, 'football', 'hide-and-seek', 'mobile games'.

sections.heading: Expressing Game Preference
sections.content: Use 'My favorite game is...' or 'I like to play...' For example: 'My favorite game is football.' or 'I like to play hide-and-seek.'

sections.heading: Simple Reasons for Liking a Game
sections.content: Give a simple reason like: 'It is fun.' 'It is exciting.' 'I play with my friends.' For example: 'I like football because it is fun.'

sections.heading: Mention Who You Play With
sections.content: You can add who you play with. 'I play with my friends.' 'I play with my brother.'

mcqQuestions.stemText: Which word describes a game that makes you happy?
My favorite game _____ chess.
I like to _____ games with my friends.

speakingTasks.prompt: Talk about your favorite game. What is its name? Is it an indoor or outdoor game? Who do you usually play it with? Speak for 30-45 seconds.
Describe why you like your favorite game. What makes it fun or interesting for you? Speak for 30-45 seconds.

lessons.title: Describe Your Room
lessons.description: Learn to describe your own room, including the furniture and objects in it.

sections.heading: Pronouncing Room and Furniture Names
sections.content: Practice 'room', 'bed', 'desk', 'chair', 'window'. Pay attention to the 'oo' sound in 'room' and 'window'.

sections.heading: Describing Objects in Your Room
sections.content: Use 'In my room, there is a...' or 'I have a...' For example: 'In my room, there is a bed and a desk.' or 'I have a blue chair.'

sections.heading: Use Prepositions for Location
sections.content: Use simple prepositions like 'on', 'in', 'next to' to say where things are. For example: 'My book is on the desk.' or 'My bed is next to the window.'

sections.heading: Mention Colors of Objects
sections.content: Combine colors with objects. 'My bed is brown.' 'I have a white lamp.'

mcqQuestions.stemText: What do you sleep on in your bedroom?
There _____ a window in my room.
My books are _____ the shelf.

speakingTasks.prompt: Describe your room. What color are the walls? Name two pieces of furniture you have in your room. Speak for 30-45 seconds.
Talk about your favorite item in your room. What is it? Where is it? Why do you like it? Speak for 30-45 seconds.

lessons.title: Talk About a Weekend Activity
lessons.description: Learn to describe what you do on the weekend and express your enjoyment.

sections.heading: Pronouncing 'Weekend' and Activity Verbs
sections.content: Practice 'weekend' (stress on the first syllable) and verbs like 'play', 'visit', 'watch', 'read'. Ensure clear 'd' and 't' sounds.

sections.heading: Talking About Weekend Plans
sections.content: Use 'On the weekend, I usually...' or 'Last weekend, I...' For example: 'On the weekend, I usually visit my grandparents.' or 'Last weekend, I played football.'

sections.heading: Use Simple Adverbs of Frequency
sections.content: Use 'usually' or 'sometimes' to describe how often you do an activity. 'I usually play games.' 'Sometimes I read books.'

sections.heading: Express Enjoyment Simply
sections.content: Say 'It is fun.' 'I like it.' 'I enjoy it.' For example: 'Visiting my grandparents is fun.'

mcqQuestions.stemText: Which day is part of the weekend?
On the weekend, I usually _____ my friends.
I like to _____ TV with my family on Sunday.

speakingTasks.prompt: Describe one activity you usually do on the weekend. What is it? Who do you do it with? Speak for 30-45 seconds.
Talk about your favorite weekend activity. Why do you like it? What makes it special for you? Speak for 30-45 seconds.

lessons.title: Describe a Photo
lessons.description: Learn to describe what you see in a simple photo using basic vocabulary and prepositions.

sections.heading: Pronouncing 'Photo' and Object Names
sections.content: Practice 'photo' (stress on the first syllable) and names of common objects or people you might see. Ensure clear 'o' sounds.

sections.heading: Starting Your Description
sections.content: Use 'In this photo, I see...' or 'This is a photo of...' For example: 'In this photo, I see a family.' or 'This is a photo of my friends.'

sections.heading: Use 'There is/are' and Prepositions
sections.content: Say what is in the photo and where. 'There is a dog in the photo.' 'The boy is next to the girl.' 'The ball is on the grass.'

sections.heading: Mention Colors and Simple Actions
sections.content: Describe colors of objects or clothes. 'The girl has a red dress.' Mention simple actions. 'They are playing.'

mcqQuestions.stemText: What do you use to take a photo?
In the photo, there _____ two children.
The cat is _____ the table.

speakingTasks.prompt: Imagine you have a photo of your family. Describe who is in the photo and one thing they are doing. Speak for 30-45 seconds.
Imagine you have a photo of a park. Describe two things you see in the park and their colors. Speak for 30-45 seconds.

lessons.title: Numbers in Daily Life
lessons.description: Learn to use numbers to talk about age, quantity, and simple measurements.

sections.heading: Pronouncing Numbers 1-20
sections.content: Practice saying numbers clearly, especially 'thirteen' vs 'thirty' and 'fourteen' vs 'forty'. Focus on the 'teen' ending for numbers 13-19.

sections.heading: Using Numbers for Age and Quantity
sections.content: For age: 'I am [number] years old.' For quantity: 'I have [number] books.' or 'There are [number] apples.' For example: 'I am 10 years old.' 'I have two brothers.'

sections.heading: Count Objects Around You
sections.content: Look around and count things: 'I see three pens.' 'There are two windows.' This helps with fluency.

sections.heading: Use Numbers for Simple Information
sections.content: You can also use numbers for phone numbers (say digits individually) or house numbers. 'My house number is 12 (one-two).'

mcqQuestions.stemText: How many fingers do you have on one hand?
I am _____ years old.
There are _____ days in a week.

speakingTasks.prompt: Talk about yourself using numbers. Say your age, how many people are in your family, and how many pets you have (if any). Speak for 30-45 seconds.
Look around your room. Count and describe the number of two different types of objects (e.g., 'I have three books.'). Speak for 30-45 seconds.

lessons.title: Talk About Your Morning
lessons.description: Learn to describe your morning routine and activities using simple time expressions.

sections.heading: Pronouncing Morning Activities
sections.content: Practice verbs like 'wake up', 'get dressed', 'eat breakfast', 'go to school'. Focus on clear articulation of each word.

sections.heading: Sequencing Morning Events
sections.content: Use 'In the morning, I...' and 'Then, I...' For example: 'In the morning, I wake up at 6 o'clock. Then, I brush my teeth and eat breakfast.'

sections.heading: Use 'at' for Specific Times
sections.content: When talking about specific times, use 'at'. 'I wake up at 6 AM.' 'I eat breakfast at 7 o'clock.'

sections.heading: Keep it Chronological
sections.content: Describe your morning activities in the order they happen. This helps with flow and makes it easier for others to understand.

mcqQuestions.stemText: What is the first meal of the day?
I usually _____ up at 6 AM.
Before school, I _____ my teeth.

speakingTasks.prompt: Describe your morning routine. What time do you wake up? What two things do you do after waking up? Speak for 30-45 seconds.
Talk about your favorite part of the morning. What do you do then, and why do you like it? Speak for 30-45 seconds.

lessons.title: Describe a Simple Story
lessons.description: Learn to tell a very simple story or sequence of events using basic past tense verbs.

sections.heading: Using Simple Past Tense
sections.content: For A1, focus on common irregular verbs like 'went' (go), 'saw' (see), 'ate' (eat), 'had' (have). Practice saying them clearly.

sections.heading: Starting and Continuing a Story
sections.content: Use 'Yesterday, I...' or 'Last weekend, I...' Then, use 'and then...' or 'After that...' For example: 'Yesterday, I went to the park. And then, I saw a dog. After that, I went home.'

sections.heading: Keep Sentences Short and Clear
sections.content: Don't try to make complex sentences. Focus on one event per sentence. 'I went to the market. I bought some fruit. I came home.'

sections.heading: Use Time Markers
sections.content: Words like 'yesterday', 'last night', 'last weekend' help set the scene for your story.

mcqQuestions.stemText: The past tense of 'go' is _____.
Yesterday, I _____ a movie.
Last night, I _____ dinner with my family.

speakingTasks.prompt: Tell a short story about what you did last weekend. Mention two or three simple actions you did. Speak for 30-45 seconds.
Describe a simple story about going to a specific place (e.g., the park, the market). What did you see there? What did you do? Speak for 30-45 seconds.

lessons.title: Your Favorite Place
lessons.description: Learn to describe your favorite place and explain why you like it.

sections.heading: Pronouncing Place Names
sections.content: Practice saying names of common places like 'park', 'beach', 'library', 'home'. Ensure clear vowel sounds.

sections.heading: Expressing Preference for a Place
sections.content: Use 'My favorite place is...' or 'I like [place] very much.' For example: 'My favorite place is the park.' or 'I like the beach very much.'

sections.heading: Describe What You Do There
sections.content: Mention simple activities you do at your favorite place. 'I play with my friends at the park.' 'I read books at the library.'

sections.heading: Give Simple Reasons for Liking It
sections.content: Use adjectives like 'beautiful', 'quiet', 'fun', 'relaxing'. 'The park is beautiful.' 'It is a fun place.'

mcqQuestions.stemText: Which place has many books?
My favorite place _____ the beach.
I like to _____ at the park.

speakingTasks.prompt: Describe your favorite place. What is it? Where is it (e.g., in your city, near your home)? What does it look like? Speak for 30-45 seconds.
Talk about why your favorite place is special to you. What do you like to do there, and how does it make you feel? Speak for 30-45 seconds.

lessons.title: Greet Someone New
lessons.description: Practice greeting someone new and asking basic questions to start a simple conversation.

sections.heading: Intonation for Questions
sections.content: For 'What's your name?' or 'How are you?', your voice usually goes down at the end. For 'Are you a student?', it goes up. Practice this rise and fall.

sections.heading: Basic Greetings and Questions
sections.content: Use: 'Hello, my name is [Your Name]. What's your name?' 'Nice to meet you.' 'How are you?' For example: 'Hello, I'm Lan. What's your name?'

sections.heading: Listen Carefully to the Reply
sections.content: When someone answers, try to listen for their name and a simple answer to 'How are you?'. This shows you are engaged.

sections.heading: Smile and Make Eye Contact
sections.content: A friendly smile and looking at the person (if culturally appropriate) help you seem confident and welcoming, even if your English is basic.

mcqQuestions.stemText: What is a common response to 'How are you?'
When you meet someone, you say 'Nice to _____ you.'
What is the correct question to ask about someone's well-being?

speakingTasks.prompt: Imagine you are meeting a new person. Greet them, introduce yourself, and ask their name. Speak for 30-45 seconds.
Imagine you have just met someone new. After introducing yourselves, ask them 'How are you?' and one simple follow-up question (e.g., 'Are you a student?'). Speak for 30-45 seconds.

lessons.title: Talk About Today
lessons.description: Learn to talk about what you are doing today and how you feel.

sections.heading: Using 'Today' Clearly
sections.content: Practice saying 'today' (stress on the second syllable). Ensure the 'ay' sound is clear.

sections.heading: Describing Today's Activities
sections.content: Use 'Today, I am...' or 'I am [verb+ing] today.' For example: 'Today, I am studying English.' or 'I am going to school today.'

sections.heading: Expressing Feelings
sections.content: You can say 'I am happy today.' 'I am tired today.' or 'I am good.' This adds a personal touch.

sections.heading: Mention the Weather
sections.content: A simple way to add more to your description is to mention the weather. 'Today, it is sunny.' 'It is cold today.'

mcqQuestions.stemText: What is the opposite of 'yesterday'?
Today, I _____ learning English.
I am feeling _____ today. I have a lot of energy.

speakingTasks.prompt: Talk about today. What day of the week is it? What is the weather like? Mention one thing you are doing today. Speak for 30-45 seconds.
Describe how you are feeling today and why (one simple reason). What is one activity you are looking forward to doing today? Speak for 30-45 seconds.
